title: Nintendo Doesn't Care About GTA 6: Zelda Switch 2 Remake Timing Explored
description: Polygon reports that Nintendo's release date for The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Switch 2 remake is surprisingly close to GTA 6.
author: GTA6 Hub Editorial
content:
## Nintendo's Bold Scheduling Approach

In the modern gaming landscape, Rockstar Games' upcoming blockbuster *GTA 6* casts a massive shadow over the release calendar. Most publishers and developers go to great lengths to avoid launching their heavy-hitters anywhere near a title of that magnitude. However, according to a recent report by gaming media outlet Polygon, Nintendo's internal plans suggest a different attitude entirely.

## A Surprisingly Close Window

Polygon highlighted that Nintendo's planned release date for *The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time* Switch 2 remake is actually much closer to the launch window of *GTA 6* than most industry observers would dare to anticipate. While avoiding direct clashes with the Grand Theft Auto franchise has long been an unwritten rule for maximizing sales, Nintendo's scheduling choice implies an intriguing level of confidence in both the Switch 2 ecosystem and the enduring appeal of the Zelda franchise.

## Independent Market Strategies

While both franchises represent the absolute pinnacle of interactive entertainment, they operate within distinct hardware ecosystems and target unique player behaviors. Nintendo has historically charted its own course, focusing on first-party momentum and platform-exclusive experiences rather than reacting defensively to third-party monoliths. Whether this timing stems from strict development milestones or a calculated counter-programming strategy, it certainly disrupts the conventional wisdom of game release calendars.

## Editor's Take

Nintendo's apparent indifference to the scheduling gravity of *GTA 6* highlights the unique position the company holds in the industry. By betting on the timeless pull of *Ocarina of Time* on new hardware, Nintendo proves once again that it plays by its own rules, completely unbothered by outside industry blockbusters.
